title: Edge admin delegation sandbox - PRD (rough)
summary: This PRD proposes a lightweight, customer-sandboxed delegation and staged-approval experience for customer-managed networking changes. The feature pairs an isolated operator sandbox (where customer operators can compose and validate change bundles) with a configurable approval gate that emits compact, tamper-evident audit artifacts to Redwood's control plane. The goal is to reduce operational friction for enterprise customers that must keep control of network configuration while still enabling Redwood to provide safety checks, telemetry, and reversible rollouts.
goals: 1) Give customers a safe place to prepare and simulate VPC/edge config changes before applying. 2) Provide a standardized approval gate that supports multi-actor signoffs and automated policy checks. 3) Emit compact, verifiable audit payloads (signed receipts + diffs) that satisfy common compliance needs without overwhelming retention budgets. 4) Integrate with Private deployments' operator UX and existing attestation telemetry.
non_goals: 1) Not implementing full NTD (network change) enforcement at the host OS level — this is a change orchestration and evidence pipeline. 2) Not replacing customer's native firewall or router CLIs. 3) Not building a general-purpose RBAC system — scope is operator delegation tied to change bundles and approval gates.
background: Enterprise customers running private deployments require strong change provenance for networking: who requested what, what was validated, and what evidence exists if something goes wrong. Current customer feedback: handoffs are error-prone, operators maintain ad-hoc spreadsheets for approvals, and security teams ask for compact artifacts rather than full pcap-like telemetry. There are several adjacent Redwood efforts (attestation bundles, proof-of-change ledger prototypes, approval-sim harness) — this PRD ties them into a coherent UX and rollout path focused on operator experience and audit artifact sizing.
user_personas:
- Platform Operator (customer): prepares VPC or edge changes, wants safe validation and a way to request signoffs.
- Security Reviewer (customer): reviews change bundles, verifies policies, and approves/rejects.
- Redwood Operator (support): can inspect evidence artifacts, offer guided rollbacks, and troubleshoot.
- Product Admin (Redwood): configures per-customer gate policies and retention tiers.
success_metrics:
- Reduction in mean time from change draft to applied change by 35% for pilot customers.
- 90% of change bundles include a valid compact audit artifact after rollout.
- Support tickets related to ambiguous change provenance reduced by 50% in first 3 months.
- Pilot customers opt into automated policy checks for at least 60% of their change bundles.
core_requirements: 1) Sandbox: lightweight UI and CLI where operators compose 'change bundles' (YAML diffs). Bundles include metadata: author, timestamp, component targets, pre-apply checks. 2) Simulation: dry-run that executes compatibility and dependency checks against a customer-managed simulator or lightweight validation agent. Results produce a structured report. 3) Approval Gate: policy-configurable flows supporting sequential and parallel signoffs, optional automatic approvers (policy bots), and timeboxed expirations. 4) Evidence Artifacts: compact JSON payloads containing bundle diff, validation report summary, approver signatures (user id + time + signature token), and optional cryptographic digest. Payload size must be capped (recommendation: default 64KB, configurable). 5) Immutable Audit Store: Redwood control plane accepts artifacts and stores an indexable summary; full artifacts optionally exported back to customer's storage. Retention tiers (30d/180d/7y) must be supported via product settings. 6) Integration hooks: webhooks, S3 export, SIEM syslog forwarder, and a read-only API for auditors. 7) Access Controls: operator sandbox can be shared within customer teams with link-level roles: draft-only, reviewer, approver, and readonly. 8) Rollback helpers: from artifact, generate a deterministic reversal bundle and provide a manual rollback workflow for operators.
approval_flow_sketch: 1) Operator creates bundle in sandbox -> generates dry-run report. 2) Operator selects approvers (team or role). 3) Gate enforces prechecks and publishes artifact to Redwood control plane. 4) Approvers receive a summarized review card (in UI and email/SIEM) with one-click approve/reject. 5) After required signoffs, change transitions to 'scheduled-apply' or 'apply-now' based on operator choice. 6) Post-apply, an applied artifact is emitted with results and verification checks. 7) Any failed verification triggers automated rollback path if enabled.
audit_log_spec:
- Minimal index schema: artifact_id, bundle_id, customer_id, summary_hash, created_by, create_ts, policy_tags, status, retention_tier.
- Artifact payload: base64 gzipped JSON containing: bundle_diff, validation_summary, approvers[], signatures[], apply_result (success/failure), revert_bundle (optional).
- Signing model: rely on customer SSO user ids and Redwood short-lived signing tokens; signatures are HMACs using per-customer key stored in KMS.
- Size & cost controls: warn users when artifact > 64KB; require explicit confirmation for >256KB.
- Query surface: time-range, bundle_id, approver, status, policy_tag.
- Export APIs: bulk export by time-range + incremental cursor to customer S3 or support team bucket.
ux_considerations:
- Provide condensed review cards: top-line diff (human-friendly), 2–3 critical validation failures, and link to full artifact.
- Mobile/Email: enable single-click approval links that open a secure ephemeral review session.
- Sandbox UX: quick-create from templates, ability to import existing infra-as-code snippets.
- Visual indicators for retention tier and whether artifact contains 'sensitive' fields (masking recommendations).
- Undo affordance: clearly surface whether automatic rollback is enabled and who can trigger it.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (Q2 pilot): internal alpha with two strategic customers; manual artifact ingestion and export.
Phase 1 (Q3 limited beta): add approval gate automation, retention tiers, SIEM export.
Phase 2 (Q4 public beta): RBAC polish, mobile approvals, bulk export API.
Phase 3 (next year): encryption-at-rest enhancements, HSM-backed signing, and formal compliance pack for SOC/ISO audits.
dependencies:
- Attestation bundles service (research/proto).
- Short-lived signing tokens & per-customer KMS keys.
- Sandbox validation agent (lightweight) from infra team.
- Console UI work in product-console.
- SIEM/syslog export infra under observability team.
open_questions:
- Do customers want canonical cryptographic signatures (HSM-backed) in MVP or is HMAC acceptable?
- What is the right default artifact size cap that balances evidence fidelity with storage cost?
- Should Redwood offer a hosted artifact archive for long-term retention or only export hooks?
- How do we integrate with customers that run fully air-gapped private deployments?
- Do legal/compliance teams require certificate chains or just user-level signatures for audits?
